title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review end-to-end benchmark results (latency & throughput) versus customer baseline provider. Discussed tuning levers (batching, quantization, KV/prefix caching), infra differences, and next steps for a cleanup run and security docs. Agreed to run 2 additional tests with adjusted batch and q8 profiles and schedule a follow-up demo of private deployment options.

Prefix/KV cache effect on tail latency
Next steps: additional benchmark runs, security docs, pricing follow-up

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (NovaTech Head of ML), Sara Lopez (Platform Eng), Mike Chen (CTO)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — benchmark review vs the baseline provider, dig into the p95/p99, talk tuning levers, then next steps. Priya will run through the numbers.
[00:22] Priya: Cool, I put the spreadsheet link in the chat — redwood.ai/benchmarks/nova-2026 (note: placeholder link). We ran the same request set you sent plus the synthetic tail runs. High level: under hosted config with q4-hybrid and batch=8 we saw median latency of ~120ms per token and p95 of 420ms. Baseline provider numbers you shared show median ~140ms and p95 ~600ms. Throughput wise, at 8 concurrent workers we got ~2.4k toks/sec vs baseline 1.7k toks/sec.
[01:05] Daniel: Okay those numbers look promising. Quick question — were the baseline runs on the same model variant? They used a 70B-ops model alt, I think.
[01:12] Priya: Not exactly identical, we normalized for model size. Baseline was on CloudVendorX managed endpoint with default batch settings; we replicated request size distribution and used our q4-hybrid profile to be apples-to-apples. There is some variance due to kernel selection and seq len.
[01:30] Mike: I'm especially concerned about tail latency — p99 matters for user experience. You said p95 420ms, what's p99?
[01:36] Priya: p99 around 1.2s on the hosted run. We dug into traces and found spikes correlate with cache misses — when prefix/KV cache misses happen we load KV pages and kernel fallback causes a bump.
[01:55] Sara: When you say KV cache, is that the same as our in-process cache we run on prem? I want to map to our infra.
[02:02] Priya: Yeah similar concept; Redwood runtime keeps an LRU of prefix KV and supports serving from cache across requests when sessions reuse context. On Dedicated it gets better because the cache is warm and you avoid cross-VM misses.
[02:18] Alex: Important point — for NovaTech's production pattern you showed, reuse is high, so effective tail latency should be lower in longer sessions. But we still need to test cold-start scenarios and high-concurrency spikes.
[02:35] Daniel: About throughput: you ran batch=8. We usually run variable batching on our end; what's the tradeoff when increasing batch?
[02:42] Priya: Increase batch to 16 or 32 gives better token throughput but increases median latency. In our tests batch=16 with q8-fast yielded median 150ms per token but p95 moved to ~650ms. However throughput jumped to ~3.6k toks/sec. So it depends on your SLO — prefer lower latency or higher throughput/cost efficiency.
[03:05] Mike: How did accuracy look with q8-fast vs q4-hybrid? Any hallucination delta?
[03:10] Priya: We ran the eval set — q8-fast had a minor drop on some tight QA prompts (~1.3% lower exact match) compared to q4-hybrid. For most generation tasks it's within tolerance but call that out if you have strict ML metric gates.
[03:25] Sara: Network-wise, will VPC private deployment reduce those KV misses? Or is that independent?
[03:30] Priya: VPC per se doesn't change KV cache hit rate; it just lets you pin models to dedicated pools and reduce cross-tenant noise. Dedicated pools plus pinned model shards mean more warmed caches and better consistency.
[03:45] Daniel: Any difference in autoscaling behavior vs baseline provider? We saw baseline had slower scale-up under sudden spikes.
[03:52] Priya: Redwood's Dedicated autoscaler supports fast warm-up for reserved pools and burst capacity policy — we can configure headroom to absorb spikes. Hosted has more conservative autoscale but you can opt for burst reservations. That said, baseline's slow scale-up explains some of their p99 spikes.
[04:10] Alex: I want to call out an artifact: we noticed one of the baseline runs had degraded perf likely due to node contention; the notebook shows kernel preemption at 03:18 of that run. We annotated that on the spreadsheet.
[04:25] Daniel: Perfect. A few clarifying Qs: (1) can you reproduce the exact baseline environment (same CPU/GPU family)? (2) do you have KMS/HSM details for Private?
[04:35] Priya: For (1) we approximate hardware class; exact vendor kernels differ but we can run a baseline VM match for a clean comparison. For (2) yes — we support KMS integration and HSM options for Private; Alex will share the security pack.
[04:55] Mike: Is there an expected cost delta at similar throughput? Baseline pricing model was per-inference plus infra.
[05:02] Alex: Initial rough numbers show Redwood hosted costs are competitive at this workload due to higher efficiency; Dedicated gives predictable unit cost and lower tail at scale. We'll send a modeled TCO for the runs you care about.
[05:20] Priya: Going back to tuning — we propose two follow ups: Test A: q8-fast, batch=16, concurrency sweep 4/8/16. Test B: q4-hybrid, batch=8 with warmed cache simulation. We'll include cold-start traces as well.
[05:38] Daniel: That sounds good. Can you also include a run with constrained network egress to simulate our on-prem gateway?
[05:45] Priya: Yep we can throttle egress to emulate that.
[05:50] Sara: For the evaluation metrics, please include median, p95, p99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:58] Priya: Affirmative — we'll add cost per token and per-1M.
[06:05] Alex: Quick note, we saw a golden path where with cache-warmed Dedicated and q4-hybrid you get p95 ~300ms and p99 ~700ms for your typical session pattern. We'll highlight that in the sheet.
[06:20] Mike: Any concerns about model compatibility if we want to move to Private on prem?
[06:25] Priya: Private supports the same model variants we used in hosted; some quantized kernels are more mature on certain GPUs. We'll call out any model/hardware mismatches.
[06:38] Daniel: Are there any security review blockers? We need SOC2 + pen test report.
[06:44] Alex: We'll send SOC2, ISO docs, and a redwood-private-arch note. Expect that by EOD tomorrow.
[06:54] Daniel: Great.
[07:00] [longer silence as participants look at spreadsheet link]
[07:20] Priya: I'm posting a summary of the 6 highlighted runs: hosted q4-hybrid batch8, hosted q8-fast batch16, dedicated warm q4 batch8, baseline-provided run A, baseline run B (no cache), cold-start synthetic. Each row has median/p95/p99/toks-per-sec/cost.
[07:50] Sara: I see the dedicated warm q4 looks best for our interactive flow. What's the expected uplift in cost?
[07:58] Alex: Dedicated will have a fixed reserved cost; we modeled per-token unit cost — effective per-token cost dropped ~18% at your 1M tok/month level vs hosted because of improved throughput. We'll attach TCO slide.
[08:15] Daniel: For acceptance criteria, we care about p95 under 500ms for interactive and cost delta less than 20% vs baseline — can Redwood meet that in Dedicated?
[08:25] Priya: Based on today's runs, yes, Dedicated warm config meets p95 ~300-400ms. We'll run sanity checks to ensure that's repeatable.
[08:36] Mike: Let's talk timeline: if we get two confirmation runs next week and security docs, we could kick off a 30-day pilot in Oct.
[08:44] Alex: Sounds good, we'll target the tests early next week.
[08:50] Daniel: Any blockers from our side? We'll need to allocate Sara and a network engineer for the VPC test and share request traces.
[08:58] Sara: I'll schedule and provide the trace by Friday.
[09:05] Alex: Recap of next steps: Redwood runs two focused tests, Priya posts results to spreadsheet, Alex sends security + TCO, customer uploads traces and confirms VPC constraints. Schedule follow-up the week of Sep 21.
[09:25] Mike: Thanks everyone.
[09:28] Alex: Thanks, bye.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: there are small speaker attribution swaps and a few mis-typed acronyms (KV written as K V at times). Natural speech patterns and filler words preserved.
